## Equivalence

Overall: **PASSED** (full workload).

| workload | N_max legacy / new | descriptors: max abs diff (violations) | energies, same weights: max abs / rel diff | passed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2000× aspirin-like | [20, 11] / [20, 11] | local_matrix 0.0e+00 (0), local_numbers 0.0e+00 (0), long_range_matrix 0.0e+00 (0), long_range_features 0.0e+00 (0) | 2.67e-05 / 1.0e-06 (\|E\| ≤ 42, 0 violations) | yes |
| 200× stachyose-like | [85, 58] / [85, 58] | local_matrix 0.0e+00 (0), local_numbers 0.0e+00 (0), long_range_matrix 0.0e+00 (0), long_range_features 0.0e+00 (0) | 7.63e-05 / 6.4e-07 (\|E\| ≤ 136, 0 violations) | yes |

* Descriptors: atol = rtol = 1e-06, integer columns exact, after reordering the legacy rows (cell traversal order) into input order. Model: `legacy-head` architecture, `assignment = "legacy"`.
* Energies: legacy model built with seed, weights exported in construction order and loaded with `lrmlp.model.assign_legacy_weights`; rtol 1e-05, atol 1e-05 per atom. New energies come from `Potential.predict` (positions → descriptors → batched model).
* XLA: 100 training steps with `jit_compile=false` and `true` from the same weights and data order: max rel. weight diff 4.3e-05 (|w| > 1e-3), max abs 4.0e-06, rel. diff of the mean loss 1.5e-07 (largest per-step rel. loss diff 2.7e-04, reported only) → passed (rtol 0.0001).
* `steps_per_execution` 8 vs 1, one epoch (1600 steps): max abs weight diff 0.0e+00, rel. loss diff 0.0e+00 → passed.

## `steps_per_execution` and `jit_compile`

| steps_per_execution | jit_compile=false | jit_compile=true | XLA gain |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 289 | 543 | +88 % |
| 8 | 373 | 701 | +88 % |

Gain of `steps_per_execution = 8` over 1: +29 % without XLA, +29 % with XLA.

Rule: a default changes only with a gain of at least 15 % and a passed equivalence check (plan section 4.4). Defaults in `src/` are **not** changed by this benchmark.

* `train.jit_compile`: gain +88 % / +88 % (K = 1 / 8), equivalence passed → **recommend `jit_compile = true`** as the new default.
* `train.steps_per_execution`: gain +29 %, equivalence passed → **recommend `steps_per_execution = 8`**.

XLA compiles the step once per input shape. The atom axis is `None` in the signature, so a dataset with molecules of different sizes would compile once per size; every dataset of the thesis holds a single molecule (one shape), the benchmark as well.

<!-- BEGIN MANUAL ANALYSIS -->
### Analysis of the missed targets

All numbers on this page are **preliminary**. Other jobs were running during the
measurement (load average 5-25 on 10 CPUs, see above), so single repetitions spread
by up to 3× (`times_s` in the result files). The causes below come from profiles and
control runs; they do not depend on the exact factors.

**Preprocessing, 1 process (15× and 7× instead of 20×).** The descriptor kernel is
vectorized per molecule (`compute_descriptors`, no Python loop over atom pairs). For
the 21-atom aspirin-like molecule it needs about 0.3-0.4 ms per frame; the legacy
`create_grid` + `create_matrices` + pandas path needs about 4.3 ms. At this size a
frame is about 20 NumPy calls on tiny arrays, so the fixed per-call overhead of
NumPy dominates. Further speed-up would need vectorization *across* frames, which is
not part of the plan. For the 87-atom stachyose-like molecule, `grid.cell_aggregates`
takes about 80 % of the descriptor time (dense (N, N) · (N, 3M) products for the
centres of mass and the (cell, element) counts). These go to OpenBLAS, which
multithreads even tiny matrices. On the loaded machine that made the three
repetitions spread from 0.9 s to 2.9 s (median 2.7 s, factor 6.6×). A control run
with `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1` built the same 200 frames in 0.51 s (≈ 390 mol/s, ≈ 35×
the legacy rate) instead of 0.75 s with the default threads.

**Preprocessing with 10 processes (slower than 1 process).** This is the same cause,
multiplied: every spawned worker starts its own OpenBLAS thread pool, so 10 workers
oversubscribe the CPU. Stachyose-like with 10 workers: 25.5 s with default BLAS threads,
0.43 s with `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS=1`
(control run, same machine). `Potential.predict(n_workers=10)` is affected in the
same way (824 vs 2636 mol/s). Follow-up for `src/` (not changed here): limit the BLAS
threads to 1 inside the worker processes of `lrmlp.dataset` (environment variables
set before `spawn`, or `threadpoolctl`). Consider it for the serial path as well.

**Bytes per molecule on disk (0.45× instead of ≥ 3× smaller).** The legacy pickles
are gzip-compressed, and gzip removes most of the zero padding of the legacy arrays.
The new format stores uncompressed `.npy` files on purpose, so that the splits can
be memory-mapped and read without unpacking. In RAM, which is the limiting resource
in the thesis setting (26.8 GB of legacy features for stachyose, plan section 4.1),
the new format is 8.8× (aspirin-like) and 10× (stachyose-like) smaller, so that target
is met. A compressed archive copy would fix the disk ratio but not change the
working-set size. The target is reported as missed.

**Input pipeline (1.2× instead of 10×).** The target assumed that `iterrows` dominates
the legacy pipeline. It does not: the legacy rows already hold padded float32
arrays, and one row costs about 0.14 ms, close to the per-element overhead of
`tf.data` itself. The new pipeline needs about 0.12 ms per molecule, also mostly
`tf.data` overhead (`numpy_function` read, F_i reconstruction). Construction is
faster (`load`: 0.19 s → 0.03 s), there are no pandas objects, and memory is far
lower. The input pipeline is not the bottleneck of training: at ≈ 8 700 mol/s it
delivers about 30× more molecules than the training step consumes.

**Training with the default settings (0.95× instead of 1.5×).** With |B| = 1 a step
is the forward and backward pass of one 21-atom molecule (≈ 3.5 ms). The legacy step
was already a `tf.function`, so the removed host overhead (no `tf.constant` per step,
no per-step `.numpy()`, P13-P15) is small compared with the step itself. The
remaining difference of a few percent is within the noise of this run. The plan's measures pay off only through
the two options: `steps_per_execution = 8` gives +29 %, `jit_compile = true` +88 %, and
both together 2.3× the legacy rate, which meets the target. Validation profits from
batching (5.0×).

**Inference from precomputed descriptors (9.0× instead of 10×).** This is just below
the target and within the noise of this run. Batching 256 molecules removes the
per-molecule call overhead. From positions, the descriptor computation now dominates
(≈ 4 350 mol/s for the descriptors alone vs. ≈ 8 850 mol/s for the model), and the
end-to-end rate is 15.7× the legacy `create_dataset` + `evaluate_model` path.

**Recommendation (report only, defaults unchanged).** Enable `train.jit_compile = true`
and `train.steps_per_execution = 8` (2.3× the legacy training rate, equivalence
passed). Caveats: (1) the XLA check ran with dropout 0 (profile `legacy-head`). With
dropout > 0, as in the thesis presets, XLA draws different (equally distributed)
dropout masks, so runs are not comparable bit for bit with non-XLA runs
(`lrmlp.training` docstring). (2) XLA compiles once per atom count, which costs
nothing for the single-molecule datasets of the thesis.
<!-- END MANUAL ANALYSIS -->

## Method

* **Same runtime.** Both implementations run in the same virtual environment (`.venv`,
  same TensorFlow build and thread settings). The legacy code (`Neural-Network/` at
  commit `9413bfd`, unchanged) is exported with `git archive` into a temporary
  directory (`tests/golden/legacy.py`) and runs in its own process with
  `TF_USE_LEGACY_KERAS=1` (tf_keras); `lrmlp` runs in a separate process with Keras 3.
* **Workloads.** Deterministic synthetic molecules from `tests/golden/synthetic.py`
  (Lennard-Jones energies): 2000 aspirin-like frames (21 atoms, grid G-A: Δg = 1 Å,
  l_max = 6) and 200 stachyose-like frames (87 atoms, G-C: Δg = 2 Å, l_max = 4);
  `--quick` uses 200 / 20. Both processes generate the same arrays (checked by a
  SHA-256 over E, F, R, z).
* **Profile.** Grid assignment `legacy` and the network of `configs/legacy-head.toml`
  (embedding 64-128-128-128, K1 = 30 / 6, K2 = 4 / 2, fitting 128 + 2 residual blocks,
  dropout 0) for both implementations; N_max is taken from the data. Split 0.8 / 0.1 /
  0.1, shuffle buffer 1000.
* **Timing.** `time.perf_counter`, median of at least 3 repetitions (`--repeats`).
  Preprocessing: whole `create_dataset` / `build_dataset` call. Input pipeline: one
  pass over the training split without a model (after one warm-up pass; dataset
  construction reported separately as `load`). Training: one warm-up epoch, then 3
  windows of 2 epochs on the same model, energy loss only, one molecule per step
  (|B| = 1). Inference: 1000 molecules; legacy as in `evaluate.py` (one
  `tf.function` call per molecule on the preprocessed test pickle), new with
  `Potential.predict_descriptors` / `Potential.predict` and `batch_size = 256`.
* **Observation hooks.** The legacy code is not modified. For the training and
  inference loops the dataset returned by `create_tf_dataset` is wrapped by an
  iterator that records time stamps, and `Training.get_model` is replaced by a call of
  the unchanged `Model.get_model` after `clear_session()` and a fixed seed.

## Mixed precision

Mixed precision is not used and not benchmarked (plan section 4.4). The molecule energy
is the sum of the atomic energies and has a magnitude of |E| ≈ 4·10⁵ kcal/mol for
aspirin. float16 overflows at 65 504; bfloat16 has 8 significand bits, i.e. a
resolution of about 2·10³ kcal/mol at that magnitude, three orders of magnitude above
the target MAE of ≈ 1.7 kcal/mol. A loss-scaling optimizer does not help, because the
problem is the representable precision of the summed energy, not gradient underflow.

## Scope

Training with more than one molecule per optimizer step (|B| > 1) is not part of this
benchmark and not part of the code: the thesis trains with |B| = 1 (p. 51) and names
larger batches as future work (Chapter 7.4). The batched paths measured here
(validation, inference) do not change the result, only the number of model calls.

## Reproducing

```sh
source .venv/bin/activate
python benchmarks/run_benchmarks.py --impl new --suite all --out NEW.json
TF_USE_LEGACY_KERAS=1 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    python benchmarks/run_benchmarks.py --impl legacy --suite all --out LEGACY.json
python benchmarks/compare.py LEGACY.json NEW.json --check-equivalence --markdown docs/benchmarks.md
```

Runtime of the runs on this page: legacy 143 s, new
218 s, plus the equivalence check. See
`benchmarks/README.md`.
